description: Tutorial T1 step 7/13 ('READ DA BAR!', pad-only) must not be a dead end. Reported: the player is on the Battlewagon from step 3, cycles off it with RB onto the embarked Boyz + Warboss, presses A to Continue and NOTHING happens — the bumper had popped the Disembark dialog (a native-nav modal that then owns A), or, with the virtual cursor awake, A was a synthetic board click on a unit with no models on the table. The only feedback was 'Oi! Not dat one, ya git — READ DA BAR!', which never said what WOULD work. This scenario boots the lesson on a pad, walks to the ack step, and asserts: the hint bar advertises 'A Continue' (and no longer 'Cycle Units'), the card names the button, LB/RB refuse to cycle and toast an instruction that names Continue, and A advances the step from anywhere on screen — cursor awake, focus released, whatever the selection is.

steps.comment: the step under test is device:'pad' — on mouse+keyboard it is skipped entirely. Every act from here on is pad input; a stray mouse click would re-claim KBM and skip it.
walk to the step under test with the card's own Skip Step handler (the button itself is FOCUS_NONE, so the pad cannot reach it). Navigation only — nothing here is the thing being validated.
step 7 of 13 on a pad (steps 8-9 are the kbm-only hotkey-help pair)
the card names the button that ends the step, instead of only describing the hint bar
the bar the step tells the player to read must itself say A = Continue — and must NOT advertise Cycle Units, which is the affordance that led into the dead end
RB — the reported first wrong turn: cycle off the Battlewagon

steps.script:
var mc = tree.current_scene.get("movement_controller")
return "none" if mc == null else str(mc.active_unit_id)
steps.comment: the bumpers stand down on an ack step, so the selection cannot move onto the embarked Boyz + Warboss
and therefore the Disembark dialog never opens to steal A
the refusal toast names Continue instead of echoing the bark ('READ DA BAR!'), which told the player nothing about what would work
push the stick to look around — this wakes the virtual cursor, which used to swallow A as a synthetic board click
A — must Continue, cursor awake or not
hint_bar is done; the kbm-only hotkey-help pair is skipped on a pad, so the next pad step is 10/13
